To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the anticentromere autoantibody (ACA) is associated with HLA class II DRB1*01, DQA1*05, and DQB1*05 alleles in Japanese patients with Scleroderma (SSc), and that ACA positive patients are heterogeneous in their HLA class II associations.

the anticentromere autoantibodies are associated with multiple human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) in Japanese patients with scleroderma (systemic sclerosis), and that the HLA associations with anticentrometer antibodies are different in Japanese and Caucasian patients.
the frequency of DQB1 * 0501 was significantly higher in ACA positive Scleroderma patients compared with ACA-negative Scleroderman patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HLA class II molecules in the development of autoimmune diseases and their clinical manifestations.
the development of a new method to determine the HLA class II genotype in a single reaction using a single primer set.
the study of the molecular basis of the genetic susceptibility of systemic sclerosis (SSC).

HLA-DRB1*010101*1502 is associated with low ACA titre and low CENP-C reactivity, and HLA-DR1*0101*0405 and *1302 with high ACA titre and high CENP-C.
the HLA class II association with SSc is complex, with multiple HLA genes involved.
the ACA response in Japanese is associated with multiple class II genes, including DQB1* 0501.
